question: What kind of teaching abiding in the ear is said to be heard by tradition in this address to the goddess?
premises: An address is made to the goddess.
That which abides in the ear is heard.
It is described as having come down through the order of tradition.
inference: That which abides in the ear and has come through the order of tradition is heard, O goddess.
uncertainties: The specific content of what is heard is not named here.
plain_english: That which abides in the ear, having come down through the order of tradition, is heard, O goddess.
